Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle; there is no cutaway, no insert, no second angle, no close-up. The small salesman in the loud mustard-and-plum checked suit and plum bowler, his face hidden behind an enormous waxed black moustache and small round green-tinted spectacles, stands on the saloon boardwalk holding the amber bottle up to the sun, his other hand gripping the end of the rolled rug that runs under the boots of a heavy-set customer who is already tipping over on the steps at the right. In the first three seconds he gives the rug one hard yank: it slides clean out from under the customer, who tumbles backward down the two steps and lands sitting in the dust, hat rolling away. The salesman tucks the rolled rug under his left arm, tips his bowler to the seated man with a flash of gold tooth under the moustache, bends to pick up the bulging carpet-bag with the bottle necks poking out, and walks briskly off toward the left edge of frame, glancing back once, while the customer sits in the dirt dusting off his sleeves.
